items.claim: Isa.44.23 is properly isolated as its own doxology-closure unit rather than folded into the exhortation before it.
items.evidence: The verse turns from second-person address to Jacob/Israel in Isa.44.21-22 to a pure imperative summons addressed to heavens, the depths of the earth, mountains, and forest -- a different addressee class entirely -- and the summons closes just ahead of a fresh divine self-predication that reopens under its own koh-amar construct at Isa.44.24. The disclosed rival, reading the summons as Isa.44.21-22's own closing acclamation, is a live alternative given the shared redemption vocabulary, but it does not carry the addressee shift the row's own boundary rests on.

items.claim: The Isa.44.24-28 unit is correctly bounded by two genuine divine koh-amar frame onsets, and its Cyrus-naming count is accurate.
items.evidence: Isa.44.24 opens its own creator self-predication under a fresh divine koh-amar construct and runs in one unbroken participle chain through the naming of Cyrus at Isa.44.28, immediately followed by a second, independently framed divine koh-amar construct at Isa.45.1 addressed directly to Cyrus. Cyrus is named in exactly two verses of the book, Isa.44.28 and Isa.45.1 (consonantal-skeleton sweep), both correctly placed at this two-row pair. The disclosed rival, reading Isa.44.24-45.8 as one continuous self-predication without a functionally fresh frame at 45.1, is a live, non-strawman alternative.

items.claim: The Isa.45.1-8 unit correctly holds the closing creation-imperative of Isa.45.8 inside the Cyrus commission rather than granting it a separate doxology row.
items.evidence: Isa.45.1 opens a second, independently framed divine koh-amar construct addressed directly to Cyrus in second person, in contrast to Isa.44.24-28's third-person description of him. The commission runs through the exclusive-deity formula at Isa.45.6 to the closing rain/righteousness imperative at Isa.45.8, which carries no koh-amar or addressee-shift marker of its own and so stays inside the larger frame+speech unit; the following unit opens on a fresh, verse-initial hoy at Isa.45.9. The disclosed rival, splitting Isa.45.8 off on the Isa.44.23 doxology model, is a live, non-strawman alternative given the real parallel in imperative cosmic address, but Isa.45.8 lacks the frame break that set Isa.44.23 apart from Isa.44.24.

items.claim: The Isa.45.9-10 pair is correctly held as one twinned woe unit rather than split into two atomic one-verse rows.
items.evidence: Both Isa.45.9 and Isa.45.10 open on their own verse-initial hoy exclamation and share one creator/creature metaphor -- potter and clay, then parent and child -- standing between the closing imperative of Isa.45.8 and the fresh divine koh-amar reply that opens Isa.45.11. Twinning the pair keeps a matched saying whole rather than fragmenting it below its argued bracket; the disclosed one-verse-split rival is a genuine, non-strawman alternative since each half does open on its own hoy token.

items.claim: The Isa.45.11-13 unit's trial_speech classification is honestly hedged against its own closing salvation-oracle content.
items.evidence: Isa.45.11 opens a fresh divine koh-amar construct answering the woe pair with a rhetorical rebuke of the addressee's complaint against the Maker, which grounds the trial_speech form at the row's own onset. The row discloses in one sentence that its close -- the city-building, exile-release promise of Isa.45.13 -- leans toward the salvation-oracle rival instead, and holds the classification at medium_low confidence with the frontier flag set, matching the genre tension the bytes actually carry.

items.claim: The row's label of Isa.45.14 as the 'third koh-amar frame' undercounts the divine speech-formula sequence within this span.
items.evidence: The divine koh-amar construct recurs at Isa.44.24, 45.1, 45.11, 45.14, and 45.18 within Isa.44.23-45.25 -- five onsets by the confirmed divine-frame census -- so Isa.45.14 is the fourth such onset, not the third. The undercount silently omits Isa.45.11's own onset, which this same span independently treats elsewhere as a fresh koh-amar frame answering the woe pair, without disclosing the exclusion. The boundary itself, the fresh frame opening at Isa.45.14 and the next one at Isa.45.18, is not in question; only the ordinal claim is.
tier_citations: skeleton tier (koh-amar construct census, 5 onsets named: Isa.44.24, 45.1, 45.11, 45.14, 45.18)

items.claim: The row's label of Isa.45.18 as the 'fourth koh-amar frame' undercounts the same divine speech-formula sequence.
items.evidence: By the same five-onset count -- Isa.44.24, 45.1, 45.11, 45.14, 45.18 -- Isa.45.18 is the fifth divine koh-amar onset in this span, not the fourth; the undercount again silently omits Isa.45.11. The row's actual boundary decision, the fresh addressee shift to the nations' survivors opening Isa.45.20, is independently well grounded and unaffected by the ordinal error.
tier_citations: skeleton tier (koh-amar construct census, 5 onsets named: Isa.44.24, 45.1, 45.11, 45.14, 45.18)

items.claim: The Isa.45.20-25 unit is a well-grounded trial_speech closing this run of Cyrus/creation oracles.
items.evidence: Isa.45.20 opens on a fresh imperative summons to a new addressee, those who have escaped from the nations, distinct from the offspring-of-Jacob address running through Isa.45.18-19, and the unit runs through the declare-and-witness challenge of Isa.45.21 and the universal appeal of Isa.45.22 to its closing verdict at Isa.45.25, the end of the assigned range. The disclosed rival, folding the summons into the Isa.45.18-19 self-declaration as one extended speech, is a live, non-strawman alternative given the shared exclusive-deity vocabulary, but the addressee shift is a real tier-1 marker the rival does not overcome.
